## Measured comparison

The declared NaCl model exceeds the **study-chosen $0.003RT$ benchmark** for most measured dilution enthalpies.
The signed discrepancy becomes predominantly positive at the higher temperatures.
At the highest temperature, the concentrated dilution prediction is endothermic while the reproduced measurements are exothermic.
The calculated values are caloric predictions relative to the published noncaloric fitting objectives, with historical caloric overlap only partly audited.
They support a conditional physical comparison and numerical verification of the caloric identities, without establishing uncertainty-complete physical validation.

{{< include figures/summary.md >}}

Errors are prediction minus observation, in joules per mole NaCl.
MAE is the mean absolute error; RMSE is the root-mean-square error.
The aggregate statistics weight every retained replicate equally, without treating replicates as independent experiments.
A chord is one temperature-specific initial/final molality pair.
A chord exceeds the study-chosen benchmark when at least one associated replicate has a resolved disjoint interval.
A chord overlaps only when every associated replicate overlaps; any unresolved replicate leaves the chord unresolved.

{{< include figures/signs.md >}}

The observation-centred intervals add the printed enthalpy rounding radius to the uniform benchmark.
This benchmark has no assigned confidence level and is not the experiment's complete measurement uncertainty.
The calculated intervals expand sampled extrema by empirical numerical and refinement allowances.
They are not proven continuous-input bounds.
Overlap only means that this benchmark comparison did not establish disagreement for that row.

## System, sources and model declaration

The liquid contains fully dissociated sodium and chloride in water at fixed nominal temperature and atmospheric pressure.
The [source notes](inputs/sources.md) identify the source pages, parameter history, selection and unavailable uncertainties.
The [measurement CSV](inputs/measurement-candidates.csv) retains all transcribed rows, original strings and exclusions.
Only the first three measured columns of Partanen–Partanen's supplementary dilution tables are observations; adjacent calculated error and adiabatic-temperature columns are excluded.
These are Messikomer–Wood measurements reproduced by later authors.
The original experimental numerical tables were unavailable, so the **secondary-transcription limit** remains material.
Rows above the declared molality fit domain remain in the retained inputs and exclusion list.

{{< include figures/conditions.md >}}

The [parameter declaration](inputs/parameters.json) derives from Held strategy 2, packet `/2`.
Its published objectives use density differences and osmotic behavior, including lower-temperature information for the sodium–water interaction.
No direct caloric objective is documented in those selected fits.
The complete water-parameter ancestry and possible calorimetric dependencies in compiled osmotic inputs were not reconstructed.
Consequently, **caloric overlap is only partly audited**.
No parameter, thermal function, uncertainty or source offset is fitted to the dilution measurements.

The native declaration includes the published temperature-dependent water diameter and sodium–water interaction.
The project's inferred ionic screening convention, Debye–Hückel term, unlike-ion dispersion and exclusion of same-sign ionic dispersion remain fixed.
The Born term is absent.
Malmberg–Maryott supplies a salt-independent water permittivity law.
**Its identity with the permittivity law used in the historical fit is unverified.**
The source locators and exact coefficient values are retained in the input notes and declaration.

The upper two study temperatures are a **temperature extrapolation** beyond the osmotic temperature information documented for the sodium–water law.
Temperature-dependent activity fitting constrains caloric derivatives indirectly and does not guarantee accurate second temperature derivatives.
Parameter covariance, model-form uncertainty and permittivity-derivative uncertainty are unavailable.

## Conserved-inventory caloric observables

Let $m$ be formula-unit NaCl molality and choose one mole of conserved salt, $n_s$.
The Engine counts the two ionic species separately.
With water molar mass $M_w$, the reporting inventories are

$$
n_w(m)=\frac{n_s}{M_wm},\qquad N(m)=n_w(m)+2n_s,\qquad
\mathbf x(m)=\frac{(n_w,n_s,n_s)}{N}.
$$

For native molar residual enthalpy $h^r$ or residual isobaric heat capacity $c_p^r$, define

$$
B_q(m)=\frac{N(m)q^r(m)-n_w(m)q_w^{r,*}}{n_s}.
$$

The pure-water value $q_w^{r,*}$ uses the same temperature, pressure, water parameters and liquid branch.
The apparent molar quantity also contains the ideal-gas salt-species thermal record.
Thus $B_q$ is a residual reporting combination, rather than an absolute measured apparent property.

Dilution adds pure water at the same temperature and pressure, holding salt inventory fixed:

$$
\Delta_{\rm dil}H_m
=\frac{N_fh_f-N_ih_i-(n_{w,f}-n_{w,i})h_w^*}{n_s}
=B_h(m_f)-B_h(m_i).
$$

The sign is final minus initial apparent molar enthalpy, following Pitzer–Peiper–Busey, Sec. 2, Eq. (17), printed page 4, cited in the [source notes](inputs/sources.md).
Positive dilution enthalpy is endothermic and negative is exothermic.
The two ion thermal records cancel because ion inventories are unchanged; water's ideal term cancels through the added-water balance.
The manufactured ideal records therefore supply no physical gas-ion assumption to this comparison.
Changing their full temperature functions separately verifies that cancellation.

The selected heat-capacity observable uses a finite reference molality, $m_*$:

$$
\Delta C_{p,\phi}(m,m_*)=B_{c_p}(m)-B_{c_p}(m_*),\qquad
\left(\frac{\partial\Delta_{\rm dil}H_m}{\partial T}\right)_{P,m_i,m_f}
=B_{c_p}(m_f)-B_{c_p}(m_i).
$$

This concentration difference avoids an unknown aqueous infinite-dilution heat capacity.
It does not establish absolute apparent heat capacity or measured heat-capacity accuracy.
Native pressure-closed actions include the temperature dependence of the interaction and permittivity laws.
All equation-of-state properties, association calculations and density solves run in C++; Python performs the displayed inventory combinations.

## Empirical input intervals and benchmark comparison

Each endpoint molality spans its half-last-printed-digit interval.
Temperature, pressure, parameters and the permittivity law stay fixed.
The source does not establish preparation, temperature or pressure uncertainties here; their absence is not evidence that they vanish.
The study chooses a uniform benchmark motivated by PPB's tabulated precision coefficient, without importing its unresolved concentration-dependent uncertainty prescription.
Replicates never reduce the benchmark.

For each composition, the interval calculation evaluates ordinary and tight settings with both cold and anchored starts.
The anchored seed is a cold state at the same composition and a nearby lower temperature; the pure-water seed uses its separately declared lower temperature.
All reported target properties use the target temperature and pressure.
Every request must return finite values, positive mechanical pressure slope, acceptable state/action pressure closure, available enthalpy composition actions and association diagnostics within the prescribed criterion.
The four densities must agree within the declared relative spread.
These conditions qualify the declared liquid roots, without proving global phase stability.

{{< include figures/procedure.md >}}

On each nested Cartesian grid, the tight/cold dilution values give the sampled minimum $L$ and maximum $U$.
Every sample includes all four solver/start combinations.
The empirical numerical expansion is

$$
b_{\rm num}=2E+F,\qquad
E=\max_{z,v}|D_v(z)-D_{\rm tight,cold}(z)|,
$$

$$
F=\max_{z,v}\gamma_{16}
\left(|N_fh^r_{f,v}|+|n_{w,f}h^{r,*}_{w,v}|+
      |N_ih^r_{i,v}|+|n_{w,i}h^{r,*}_{w,v}|\right).
$$

The binary64 operation allowance $γ_{16}$ uses the extensive operands before cancellation.
It does not bound internal equation-of-state error, composition-map sensitivity, or a common error shared by all four variants.
Each $B$ is evaluated as the extensive solution term minus its water term; dilution is then final $B$ minus initial $B$.

Exact native enthalpy composition actions supply the gradient of the reported dilution balance:

$$
B_h'(m)=-\frac{n_w}{m}(h^r-h_w^{r,*})+N\,\mathrm{action}_{\mathbf x'(m)}h^r,
\qquad \nabla D=(-B_h'(m_i),B_h'(m_f)).
$$

Each gradient component must keep a strict sampled sign across every variant.
Refinement stops only after two consecutive sampled-extrema changes are below the prescribed threshold, the signs agree, and the numerical expansion is small enough relative to the benchmark.
The sampling allowance is twice the larger of the last two changes.
No failed setting is replaced by a looser solve, and no further unprescribed retry occurs.

The compared intervals and nonnegative gap are

$$
I_{\rm calc}^{\rm sample}=[L-b_{\rm num}-b_{\rm sample},\ U+b_{\rm num}+b_{\rm sample}],
\qquad I_{\rm bench}=[H_{\rm obs}-u_{\rm bench}-r_H,\ H_{\rm obs}+u_{\rm bench}+r_H],
$$

$$
g=\max\{\inf I_{\rm calc}^{\rm sample}-\sup I_{\rm bench},\
\inf I_{\rm bench}-\sup I_{\rm calc}^{\rm sample},0\},\qquad
u_{\rm bench}=0.003RT.
$$

The gap has no sign and vanishes during overlap.
The separately retained signed nominal error is tight/cold prediction minus observation.
A gap exceeding twice the refinement threshold is classified as exceeding the study-chosen benchmark.
Overlap requires the signed overlap depth to exceed the same threshold.
Near-contact comparisons, failed diagnostics and unfinished sampling remain unresolved.
Finite sampling and unchanged extrema cannot prove absence of an unsampled extremum or certify the whole input rectangle.

## Numerical verification and failures

The numerical checks address conserved-inventory cancellation and exact thermal actions separately from measured agreement.
The ideal-record check changes heat-capacity coefficients and enthalpy anchors, rather than only constant offsets.
The representative dilute and concentrated chords are checked at every study temperature.

{{< include figures/identities.md >}}

The temperature finite-difference ladder only verifies the exact native action.
Its coarse and fine steps and Richardson combination are retained with the actual off-temperature balances.
They do not provide the numerical interval used for the measured comparison.
Cancellation can obscure asymptotic convergence of an already small finite-difference error.

{{< include figures/thermal-ladder.md >}}

Interval qualification requests enthalpy composition actions only.
The separate nominal enthalpy and heat-capacity temperature actions use ordinary settings.
Their higher-order association diagnostic is retained and checked against that request's criterion.
The maximum temperature-action diagnostic below includes the dilute-state derivative-coefficient value; it is not substituted into the tighter interval calculation.

## Interpretation and claim limits

The increasing positive discrepancy at higher temperatures shows that the selected model's caloric concentration dependence does not reproduce most observed dilution chords to the chosen benchmark.
The endothermic concentrated prediction at the highest temperature has the same final-minus-initial sign convention as the exothermic observations.
It is not a reversed calorimeter-heat convention.
The comparisons do not isolate a unique faulty parameter, establish an Engine defect, or authorize a refit.

The result is conditional on the fully dissociated liquid, the Held strategy-2 `/2` declaration and supplemental permittivity law.
Historical caloric overlap is only partly audited, the historical permittivity law's identity is unverified, observations are a secondary transcription, and the upper two temperatures extrapolate beyond the documented sodium–water temperature calibration.
Unknown measurement and parameter uncertainties prevent a rejection claim within complete experimental uncertainty.
No inference extends to absolute ion calorics, absolute apparent heat capacities, crystal solution enthalpies, reacting liquids, other salts or mixed solvents.
